consensus_summary: Light primarily symbolizes God’s own nature, holiness, truth, glory and presence, most fully realized in Jesus Christ as the light of the world who brings revelation, life and salvation, always set against the darkness of sin, ignorance and death; secondary but complementary applications include the word/law as guidance, moral righteousness, believers’ witness and eschatological blessing.
book_summary: Light is the law lived visibly—good works that others can see.
consensus_core_identification: God’s nature/presence (holiness, truth, glory) and Christ as the light of the world / salvation
book_core_identification: the law lived out visibly as observable good works
boundary_disagreement: Book confines the symbol exclusively to the human living of the law through visible good works, omitting or setting aside the far broader consensus range that centers on divine nature and Christ while treating law and works only as derivative applications.
material_contradiction: None; the book’s identification is already admitted within the consensus as common secondary/alternative uses rather than a denial of the primary divine/Christological referent.
rationale: Consensus cores are the divine nature and Christ; the book preserves the recognized secondary category of law-as-light plus believers’ good-works witness (explicitly supported by the same verses consensus lists for those alternatives) but narrows the entire identification to their combination—“the law lived visibly.” This is a real change of extension and precision (rejecting the wider divine cases as definitional) while remaining inside the consensus cluster, hence REFINED rather than MATCH, DIVERGENT or NOVEL.
strongest_objection: The entry elevates two secondary applications into the sole definitional core and thereby sidelines the dominant, textually primary identification of light with God’s nature and with Christ that the consensus treats as settled.
